findings.title: getCalendar does not handle dynamic import failures
findings.body: getCalendar awaits appStore[...] where each entry is now a dynamic import promise. If the app chunk fails to load, that promise rejects. The function signature and most callers expect Calendar or null and handle null, but they do not necessarily handle exceptions. Without a try/catch around the import, a missing or broken app chunk can turn an unsupported calendar into a thrown error and break booking, cancellation, or reschedule flows.

findings.title: Async calendar/video cleanup is not awaited in Reschedule
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is passed an async callback. forEach does not await those callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before remote events are actually deleted. This can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the result.

The function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before remote events are actually deleted. This can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. findings.title: Reschedule cleanup promises are fire-and-forget
findings.body: In requestReschedule, bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) is not awaited. Calendar and video deletions run in the background, errors are not caught, and sendRequestRescheduleEmail/webhooks execute before deletions complete. This can leave stale events and produce unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the deletions before sending notifications.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes are not awaited and are lost from apiDeletes
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch, credentials.forEach(async ...) is not awaited. The callback awaits getCalendar and deleteEvent and then pushes resolved values into apiDeletes, so the outer code cannot reliably wait for those deletions; apiDeletes may be incomplete when Promise.all is called. Rejections are unhandled and recurring calendar events may remain undeleted. Use Promise.all over the async work and push deletion promises instead of awaited values.

findings.title: await apiDeletes does not wait for the promises in the array
findings.body: apiDeletes is an array of promises, but awaiting the array itself does not wait for its elements or catch rejections. In the paid cancellation path, the handler can return success while calendar/video deletions are still pending or have failed. Use await Promise.all(apiDeletes) to actually wait for and propagate integration deletion errors.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar promises without an async API
findings.body: getCalendar became async, but getCalendarCredentials still calls it without await and returns objects whose calendar property is now a Promise. Only getConnectedCalendars in this file was updated to await item.calendar. Any other consumer of the exported getCalendarCredentials may now receive a Promise where it previously received Calendar or null, causing incorrect truthiness checks or runtime type errors. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await the calendars, or update and document all consumers.

findings.title: createMeeting can reject before its Cal Video fallback can run
findings.body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters outside the try/catch that implements the Cal Video fallback. Since getVideoAdapters now awaits dynamic app imports, a rejected import or app lookup will throw from createMeeting instead of triggering the fallback. Move the await into the try block or catch adapter-loading errors so fallback behavior works.

findings.title: One failing video app import aborts all video adapter operations
findings.body: getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore import without catching errors. If one credential maps to a broken or missing app module, the whole function rejects, causing getBusyVideoTimes, createMeeting, updateMeeting, or deleteMeeting to fail even for other valid credentials. Catch per-credential import errors and skip the failing adapter instead of aborting the entire operation.

findings.title: All app dynamic imports are started eagerly
findings.body: appStore calls import() for every app during module initialization. This starts loading all app chunks immediately rather than lazily loading only the requested app, and it stores promises without catch. If an import rejects before it is awaited, it can also produce an unhandled rejection. Consider lazy getters or a loader function with error handling if code-splitting and graceful failure are intended.
